paper.title: Time-varying Gaussian Process Bandit Optimization with Experts: no-regret in logarithmically-many side queries

settings.name_in_paper: Time-varying GP bandit optimization with expert side queries
unmapped: Non-stationarity measured by a per-step sup-norm variation bound sup_x |f_{t+1}(x)-f_t(x)| <= Delta = 1 (not a total variation budget)
Learner may query an external expert for noisy evaluations of the current function f_t at O(log^d t) previously observed points per round (side queries)
settings.definition_quote: We consider the problem of sequentially optimizing a reward function $f: \Dset \times \mathbb{R}_+ \to \mathbb{R}$ where $\Dset \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is a compact convex set... $y_t = f(x_t, t) + \epsilon_t$, where $\epsilon_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)$... $R_T = \sum_{t=1}^T (\max_{x} f_t(x) - f_t(x_t))$

conditions: f_t in RKHS of squared exponential kernel with k(x,x) <= M_k^2 and ||f_t||_k <= B for all t
domain is compact convex subset of R^d
learner asks an expert O(log^d t) noisy queries of f_t per time step
tuning: discard observations with injected noise variance > sigma^2 log(t)
sparse inference via approximate Q_t-DPP with Q_t = O(log^d(t/eta))

source.label: Thm:regret
source.quote: Take any $0 < \delta \leq 1$ ... Let Assumptions~\ref{as.1} and \ref{as.2} hold and consider a squared exponential kernel $k$... Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, by asking to an expert $\mathcal{O}\left(\log^d (t)\right)$ queries per time step, SparQ-GP-UCB attains a cumulative dynamic regret of $R_T = \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{ Td \log^{d+5}(T)}\sqrt{\log( \frac{1}{\delta} ) +  d \log^{d+3}( d\log(T ) )}) = \Ot(\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Regret depends on side queries to an expert, which is non-standard. Horizon marked anytime since the algorithm runs for t=1,2,... without T. beta_t uses ||f_t||_k (the RKHS norm bound). Computational complexity Theorem (Thm:complexity) O(T^2 log T log^{3d}(T/log T)) not recorded as a regret result.
